en: be promulgated; be proclaimed (of a law)

examples.en: The new law will be promulgated next month.

examples.ko: 그 문자는 오백 년 전에 반포됐어요.
examples.en: That script was promulgated five hundred years ago.
Do you remember the day the constitution was promulgated?

examples.ko: 법이 반포되면 모든 사람이 따라야 해요.
examples.en: Once a law is promulgated, everyone has to follow it.
People were surprised after the rules were announced.
The new system was promulgated and schools were informed too.

explain: '법이 반포되다'처럼 법이나 새 제도가 주어로 나오고, 사람이 주어일 때는 '반포하다'를 써요. 일상 대화에서는 거의 안 쓰고 뉴스, 역사 글, 교과서에서 만나요. 소식이 널리 알려질 때는 '알려지다'가 훨씬 자연스러워요.
explain_en: The subject is a law or a new system ('a law is promulgated'); when a person does it, use 반포하다. You will rarely hear it in conversation. It shows up in news, history writing and textbooks. For news simply becoming known, 알려지다 is much more natural.

examples.en: The government will promulgate the new law tomorrow.
The king proclaimed the new script to his people.

examples.ko: 법을 반포할 날짜가 아직 정해지지 않았어요.
examples.en: The date to promulgate the law has not been set yet.
They made the day the constitution was promulgated a holiday.

examples.ko: 관청에서 새 규칙을 반포하고 안내문도 붙였어요.
examples.en: The office announced the new rule and also put up a notice.

examples.ko: 시장님이 새 조례를 반포해서 모두 알게 됐어요.
examples.en: The mayor proclaimed the new ordinance, so everyone found out.

explain: 반포하다는 나라나 관청이 법, 문자, 새 제도를 공식적으로 세상에 알릴 때만 써요. 일상에서 소식을 전할 때는 '알리다', '발표하다'를 써요. '법을 반포하다', '헌법을 반포하다'처럼 법이나 문자와 같이 나와요.
explain_en: Use it only when a state or office officially makes a law, script or new system public. For everyday news, use 알리다 or 발표하다. It pairs with laws and scripts, as in '법을 반포하다' and '헌법을 반포하다'.

en: rewarding patriotism; honoring and supporting those who served the country (veterans' affairs)

examples.ko: 나라를 위해 싸운 분들을 위해 보훈 정책이 있어요.
examples.en: There are veterans' policies for those who fought for the country.
Many people gathered at the commemoration event.

examples.ko: 정부는 내년 보훈 예산을 올리기로 했어요.
examples.en: The government decided to raise next year's veterans' budget.
My uncle gets treatment at a veterans hospital.
June is the month of remembrance, so events are held everywhere.

examples.ko: 보훈 대상자는 여러 혜택을 받을 수 있어요.
examples.en: People eligible for veterans' support can receive various benefits.

explain: '보훈 병원', '보훈 예산'처럼 뒤에 다른 명사가 붙은 모양으로 주로 나와요. 혼자서는 잘 안 쓰고, 제도나 기관 이름 앞에서 만나요. 한국에서는 6월이 '호국보훈의 달'이라서 이 시기에 자주 들려요.
explain_en: It mostly appears in front of another noun, as in '보훈 병원' or '보훈 예산'. Alone it is uncommon; you meet it in names of systems and institutions. In Korea June is the 'month of patriots and veterans' (호국보훈의 달), so you hear it often then.

examples.en: The puppy obeys its owner well.
The soldiers obeyed the general's orders.

examples.ko: 아무 이유 없이 복종할 필요는 없어요.
examples.en: You don't have to obey for no reason.
He is not someone who bows to power.

examples.ko: 아이가 부모에게 무조건 복종하던 시대는 지났어요.
examples.en: The age when children obeyed their parents unconditionally is over.

examples.ko: 그 나라 국민들은 오랫동안 왕에게 복종하며 살았어요.
examples.en: The people of that country lived in obedience to the king for a long time.

explain: 복종하다는 힘이나 권위 앞에서 따를 수밖에 없는 느낌이 강해서, 좋은 뜻으로는 잘 안 써요. 자연스럽게 따를 때는 '따르다', 규칙에는 '지키다'가 더 편해요. 조사는 '~에/~에게 복종하다'예요.
explain_en: It carries a strong sense of following because of power or authority, so it is rarely positive. For following naturally, 따르다 is easier; for rules, 지키다. The particle is '~에' or '~에게 복종하다'.

examples.en: The nation's revival began after the war.
That city led a cultural revival.

examples.ko: 부흥을 꿈꾸던 마을 사람들이 다시 모였어요.
examples.en: The villagers who dreamed of a revival gathered again.

examples.ko: 교회 부흥 집회가 이번 주에 열려요.
examples.en: A church revival meeting is held this week.

examples.ko: 경제 부흥을 위해 새 계획을 세웠어요.
examples.en: They made a new plan for economic revival.

examples.ko: 전통 음악의 부흥에는 젊은 사람들이 큰 역할을 했어요.
examples.en: Young people played a big part in the revival of traditional music.

explain: 약해졌던 것이 다시 크게 일어날 때 써요. 그냥 '성장'과 달리 '다시'라는 느낌이 들어 있어요. '경제 부흥', '문화 부흥'처럼 나라, 도시, 분야 같은 큰 단위에 많이 써요.
explain_en: Use it when something that had weakened rises strongly again. Unlike plain 성장 (growth), it carries the feeling of 'again'. It fits big units such as a nation, a city or a field, as in '경제 부흥' and '문화 부흥'.

examples.en: This village's economy is flourishing again.

examples.ko: 전쟁이 끝난 뒤 나라가 빠르게 부흥했어요.
examples.en: After the war ended, the country revived quickly.

examples.ko: 문화가 부흥할 때는 예술가가 많이 나와요.
examples.en: Many artists appear when a culture is flourishing.
People gather in a city that is reviving.

examples.ko: 가게가 부흥하려면 손님을 먼저 생각해야 해요.
examples.en: For the shop to thrive again, you have to think of customers first.
The port that once flourished is quiet now.

explain: 한 번 약해졌던 것이 다시 일어난다는 느낌이 있어요. 처음 크는 것에는 '성장하다', '발전하다'를 써요. 주어는 사람보다 나라, 도시, 산업이 많아요.
explain_en: It implies that something once weakened is rising again. For something growing for the first time, use 성장하다 or 발전하다. The subject is more often a country, city or industry than a person.

examples.en: I completed the Korean course.
I finish the training program this month.

examples.ko: 과정을 수료하면 증명서를 받을 수 있어요.
examples.en: If you complete the program, you can get a certificate.
The students who completed the course took photos.

examples.ko: 석사 과정을 수료하고 논문을 쓰고 있어요.
examples.en: I finished the master's coursework and am writing my thesis.

examples.ko: 열 번 이상 결석하면 수료할 수 없어요.
examples.en: If you miss ten or more classes, you cannot complete it.

explain: 수료는 정해진 과정을 끝까지 마쳤다는 표현이고, 졸업은 학교의 전체 과정을 마치고 학위를 받는 거예요. 학원, 교육 과정, 대학원에는 '수료하다', 학교에는 '졸업하다'를 써요. 대학원에서 '수료'는 수업은 끝났지만 논문은 아직인 상태를 말해요.
explain_en: 수료 means you finished a set program through to the end, while 졸업 means finishing a whole school and receiving a degree. Use 수료하다 for academies, training programs and graduate school, and 졸업하다 for schools. In graduate school, 수료 means coursework is done but the thesis is not.

examples.ko: 왕이 죽은 뒤 대대적인 숙청이 있었어요.
examples.en: After the king died, there was a large-scale purge.
I read about a political purge in a history book.
To avoid the purge, he left the country.
That movie depicts the age of purges.
Reports of the purge keep appearing in the news.
The families of those purged lived hard lives.

explain: 숙청은 권력을 가진 쪽이 반대하는 사람을 몰아낼 때 쓰는 무거운 말이에요. 회사에서 사람을 줄이는 일에는 '구조조정', '정리해고'를 써요. 주로 역사나 뉴스에서 만나고, '숙청당하다'로 자주 써요.
explain_en: It is a heavy word for those in power removing their opponents. For a company cutting staff, use 구조조정 or 정리해고. You mostly meet it in history and news, often as 숙청당하다 (to be purged).

examples.en: The new king purged the ministers who opposed him.
The regime purges the people who criticize it.
The plan to purge the opposition became known.
He was a dictator who purged many subordinates.

examples.ko: 권력을 잡은 뒤 라이벌을 숙청하고 혼자 다스렸어요.
examples.en: After seizing power, he purged his rivals and ruled alone.
A scene where people are purged appears in the drama.

explain: 목적어는 사람이에요: '반대파를 숙청하다'. '쫓아내다'는 일상에서도 쓰지만, 숙청하다는 권력자가 정치적으로 제거하는 느낌이 있어요. 피동은 '숙청당하다'예요.
explain_en: The object is a person: '반대파를 숙청하다'. 쫓아내다 (kick out) is used in daily life, but 숙청하다 feels like someone in power eliminating rivals politically. The passive is 숙청당하다.

examples.en: In the old days, people offered sacrifices to the gods.

examples.ko: 신전 앞에 제물로 과일과 곡식을 올렸어요.
examples.en: They placed fruit and grain in front of the temple as offerings.

examples.ko: 그는 회사의 욕심 때문에 제물이 됐어요.
examples.en: He became a sacrificial victim because of the company's greed.

examples.ko: 개업 고사에 쓸 제물을 시장에서 샀어요.
examples.en: I bought offerings at the market for the shop-opening ritual.
There was a custom of offering cattle as a sacrifice.

examples.ko: 이 이야기에서 어린 양은 제물로 나와요.
examples.en: In this story, a young lamb appears as the offering.

explain: 제물은 제사나 종교 의식에 바치는 음식이나 동물이에요. 비유로 어떤 일의 희생양을 '제물이 되다'라고도 해요. 집에서 지내는 제사의 음식은 보통 '제수', '제사 음식'이라고 해요.
explain_en: It is what you offer at a ritual or religious ceremony. Figuratively, '제물이 되다' means becoming someone's victim. Food for ancestral rites at home is usually called 제수 or 제사 음식.

examples.ko: 산성 용액과 염기가 만나면 중화가 일어나요.
examples.en: When an acid and a base meet, neutralization happens.
We learn about neutralization reactions in science class.

examples.ko: 이 약은 위산 중화에 도움이 돼요.
examples.en: This medicine helps neutralize stomach acid.
In the experiment, we found the point where neutralization ends.
Heat is produced during the neutralization process.

examples.ko: 독소 중화 연구가 활발하게 진행되고 있어요.
examples.en: Research on neutralizing toxins is actively under way.

explain: 과학과 의학에서 쓰는 말이라 일상 대화에서는 잘 안 나와요. '중화 반응'처럼 모양이 굳은 말로 자주 보여요. '중화 요리'의 중화(中華)와 소리는 같지만 전혀 다른 말이에요.
explain_en: It belongs to science and medicine and rarely comes up in daily talk. It often appears in fixed forms like '중화 반응' (neutralization reaction). It sounds the same as 중화 in '중화 요리' (Chinese food) but is a completely different word.

examples.en: This medicine neutralizes stomach acid.

examples.ko: 염기가 산을 중화하고 물과 소금이 생겼어요.
examples.en: The base neutralized the acid, and water and salt formed.
Milk neutralizes the spicy taste.
They developed a drug that neutralizes the poison.
You can neutralize an alkali with vinegar.
I added sugar to cut the sourness.

explain: 과학에서는 산과 염기에, 일상에서는 매운맛, 신맛, 독처럼 강한 성질을 약하게 만들 때 써요. 일상 말로는 '약하게 하다', '줄이다'가 더 흔해요. 목적어를 받아서 '~을/를 중화하다'로 써요.
explain_en: In science it applies to acids and bases; in daily life, to making a strong quality like spiciness, sourness or poison weaker. In everyday speech 약하게 하다 or 줄이다 is more common. It takes an object: '~을/를 중화하다'.

examples.en: Labor exploitation is prohibited by law.

examples.ko: 그 회사는 직원 착취로 뉴스에 나왔어요.
examples.en: That company was in the news for exploiting its employees.
We must stop the exploitation of children.
The people who were exploited spoke out.
This film criticizes the exploitation by capital.

examples.ko: 정당한 월급을 주지 않는 것도 착취예요.
examples.en: Not paying a fair wage is also exploitation.

explain: '노동 착취', '아동 착취'처럼 앞에 붙는 말이 많고, 모두 강한 비판이 담겨 있어요. 일을 너무 많이 시킬 때는 '혹사시키다'도 쓰지만, 착취는 남의 노동의 이익을 가져간다는 점이 달라요. 주로 '착취를 당하다', '착취하다'로 써요.
explain_en: It often follows words like 노동 (labor) or 아동 (child), and it always carries strong criticism. 혹사시키다 also means working someone too hard, but 착취 adds the idea of taking the profit of their labor. It is mostly used as '착취를 당하다' or '착취하다'.

examples.en: The cardinal led the mass at the cathedral.
The cardinals gather to choose a new pope.

examples.ko: 한국의 한 추기경은 많은 사람에게 존경받았어요.
examples.en: A Korean cardinal was respected by many people.
People lined up to meet the cardinal.

examples.ko: 영화 속 추기경은 왕에게 조언을 해요.
examples.en: The cardinal in the movie gives advice to the king.
The cardinal visited the hospital and comforted the patients.

explain: 가톨릭에만 있는 직책이라 개신교 목사에게는 쓰지 않아요. 부를 때는 이름 뒤에 '추기경님'을 붙여 높여요. 교황을 뽑는 투표에 참여한다는 점이 주교와 달라요.
explain_en: The post exists only in the Catholic Church, so you don't use it for Protestant pastors. To address one respectfully, add '추기경님' after the name. Unlike a bishop (주교), a cardinal takes part in voting for the pope.

examples.en: Other problems arise from this problem.
A big fight arose from a small misunderstanding.
There are many words derived from English words.

examples.ko: 새 서비스가 기존 앱에서 파생해 나왔어요.
examples.en: The new service branched off from the existing app.
You have to think about the knock-on effects that follow as well.
I worried about the consequences this decision would bring.

explain: 보통 '~에서 파생하다'로 쓰고, 하나에서 갈라져 나온 것에 써요. '생기다'보다 딱딱해서 글이나 보고서에서 많이 나와요. 국어에서 '파생어'는 '덮개'처럼 어근에 접사가 붙어 만든 말이에요.
explain_en: It is usually used as '~에서 파생하다', for something that branches off from one origin. It is stiffer than 생기다 and common in writing and reports. In Korean grammar, a 파생어 is a word formed by adding an affix to a root, like 덮개.

examples.en: Air expands when it is heated.

examples.ko: 우주는 빅뱅 이후 계속 팽창되어 왔어요.
examples.en: The universe has kept expanding since the Big Bang.
The balloon swelled too much and burst.

examples.ko: 인구 증가로 도시가 팽창되면서 교통 문제가 생겼어요.
examples.en: As the city expanded because of population growth, traffic problems appeared.

examples.ko: 금속이 열에 팽창되는 정도는 재료마다 달라요.
examples.en: How much metal expands with heat differs by material.
Please explain why the budget swelled.

explain: '팽창하다'가 더 자주 쓰여요. '팽창되다'는 열이나 압력 같은 힘을 받아 부풀어 커진다는 피동의 느낌이 있어요. 반대말은 '수축되다'예요. 과학 글과 뉴스에서 만나고, 일상에서 부풀 때는 '부풀다', '커지다'가 더 자연스러워요.
explain_en: 팽창하다 is the more common form. 팽창되다 has a passive feel: something swells or grows because of a force such as heat or pressure. Its opposite is 수축되다. It appears in science writing and news; in daily life, 부풀다 or 커지다 sounds more natural.

examples.en: The mayor gave an award to the citizen who saved a person.
The school commends model students.

examples.ko: 정부가 공로가 큰 사람을 표창하기로 했어요.
examples.en: The government decided to honor people with great merit.

examples.ko: 소방서는 용감한 직원을 표창하고 기념 사진도 찍었어요.
examples.en: The fire station commended the brave employee and also took a commemorative photo.

examples.ko: 표창할 사람을 추천해 달라는 공문이 왔어요.
examples.en: An official notice came asking us to recommend people to be commended.

examples.ko: 회사에서 우수한 직원을 표창하는 행사가 열려요.
examples.en: The company holds an event commending outstanding employees.

explain: 공을 세운 사람에게 상장이나 상을 줄 때 쓰는 공식적인 말이에요. 받는 사람은 '표창을 받다'라고 해요. 개인적으로 칭찬할 때는 '칭찬하다'를 써요.
explain_en: It is a formal word for giving a certificate or award to someone for good service. The person receiving it says '표창을 받다'. For personal praise, use 칭찬하다.

examples.ko: 아이들은 별이 가득한 하늘을 보고 경이를 느꼈어요.
examples.en: The children felt wonder at the sky full of stars.
That record was a marvel even to scientists.

examples.ko: 경이의 눈으로 세상을 바라보던 때가 있었어요.
examples.en: There was a time I looked at the world with wonder.
The size of the universe always comes to me as a marvel.
He spoke in a voice full of awe.
I captured the wonders of nature in a photo.

explain: 경이는 '경이롭다', '경이로운'으로 더 자주 써요. '자연의 경이', '경이를 느끼다'처럼 글에서 많이 보이고, 대화에서는 '놀랍다', '대단하다'가 더 흔해요. 그냥 놀라는 게 아니라 감탄과 존경이 섞인 놀라움이에요.
explain_en: It is used more often as 경이롭다 or 경이로운. Phrases like '자연의 경이' and '경이를 느끼다' appear mostly in writing; in conversation 놀랍다 or 대단하다 is more common. It is not mere surprise but astonishment mixed with admiration.

examples.en: People and animals coexist in the city.
Several cultures coexisted in one country.
It is a street where tradition and modernity coexist.

examples.ko: 서로 다른 의견이 공존할 수 있어요.
examples.en: Different opinions can coexist.
To coexist with neighbors, you have to consider each other.
It was a day when sadness and joy coexisted.

explain: 'A와 B가 공존하다'처럼 서로 다른 것이 한곳에 함께 있을 때 써요. '같이 살다'는 사람과 동물의 생활에 쓰지만 공존하다는 생각이나 문화 같은 개념에도 써요. '공생하다'는 서로 도움을 주고받는 관계라서 달라요.
explain_en: Use it as 'A와 B가 공존하다' when different things exist in the same place. 같이 살다 is for the living of people or animals, but 공존하다 also covers ideas and cultures. 공생하다 (symbiosis) is different: it means helping each other.

en: (traffic) control, e.g. air traffic control; also, a different word (homonym) meaning the government administrative system

examples.en: The airport control center guides the planes.
Air traffic controllers help planes land safely.
At a port, controlling ship traffic is important.
Because of bad weather, traffic control became difficult.

examples.ko: 교통 관제 시스템이 도로 상황을 보여 줘요.
examples.en: The traffic control system shows road conditions.
The plane took off following the control tower's instructions.

explain: 공항, 항구, 도로에서 움직임을 살펴보고 지시하는 일에 써요. '관제 센터', '관제탑', '관제사'처럼 합성어로 자주 나오고 혼자서는 잘 안 써요. '통제'는 막는 느낌이 있고, 관제는 안전하게 움직이도록 안내하는 느낌이에요.
explain_en: It refers to monitoring and directing movement at airports, ports and on roads. It mostly appears in compounds such as 관제 센터, 관제탑 and 관제사, rarely alone. 통제 often feels like restricting, while 관제 feels like guiding things to move safely.

examples.en: A stand-in actor appears in dangerous scenes.
The lead was sick, so the stand-in acted instead.
He worked as a famous actor's body double.

examples.ko: 대역을 쓴 걸 알고 관객들이 놀랐어요.
examples.en: The audience was surprised to learn a stand-in was used.

examples.ko: 드라마 제작팀이 대역을 구하는 공고를 올렸어요.
examples.en: The drama team posted a call for a stand-in.

examples.ko: 이 장면은 대역 없이 직접 찍었대요.
examples.en: I heard this scene was filmed without a stand-in.

explain: 영화와 드라마에서 '대역 배우', '대역을 쓰다'로 많이 써요. 얼굴이 안 나오는 장면이나 위험한 장면에 자주 나와요. 회사에서 일을 대신할 때는 '대신하다', '대타'를 써요.
explain_en: It is most common in film and drama, as in '대역 배우' and '대역을 쓰다', often for scenes where the face isn't shown or the action is risky. At work, when someone covers for you, use 대신하다 or 대타.

examples.en: The draw is done at random.
The songs play in random order.
We split the students into two groups at random.
Drawing numbers randomly is fair.

examples.ko: 무작위 선택이라서 누구도 결과를 알 수 없어요.
examples.en: It is a random pick, so no one can know the result.
Emails were sent out at random, which caused a problem.

explain: 주로 '무작위로'나 '무작위 + 명사'(무작위 추첨)로 써요. 일상 대화에서는 '랜덤'을 더 자주 쓰고, '무작위'는 설명이나 뉴스 말투예요. '아무렇게나'는 대충 한다는 느낌이 있어서 달라요.
explain_en: It is mostly used as '무작위로' or '무작위 + noun' (무작위 추첨, a random draw). In casual speech 랜덤 is more common; 무작위 sounds like explanations and news. 아무렇게나 means doing it carelessly, so it is different.

examples.en: Exercise is good for letting off stress.

examples.ko: 에너지 발산이 필요한 아이들은 계속 뛰어다녀요.
examples.en: Kids who need to burn off energy keep running around.

examples.ko: 감정의 발산이 필요할 때는 일기를 써요.
examples.en: When I need to let my feelings out, I write in my diary.

examples.ko: 꽃의 향기 발산은 아침에 가장 많아요.
examples.en: Flowers give off the most scent in the morning.

examples.ko: 열의 발산을 돕는 팬이 달려 있어요.
examples.en: A fan that helps release heat is attached.

examples.ko: 마음껏 소리 지르는 것도 하나의 발산이에요.
examples.en: Shouting as loud as you like is also a kind of release.

explain: '스트레스 발산'처럼 쌓인 감정이나 힘을 밖으로 풀어낼 때 가장 많이 써요. '스트레스를 풀다'가 일상 말이라면 '발산'은 조금 더 글 말투예요. 열이나 향기가 퍼질 때도 써요.
explain_en: It is most often used for letting out pent-up feelings or energy, as in '스트레스 발산'. If '스트레스를 풀다' is the everyday way to say it, 발산 sounds a bit more written. It is also used when heat or scent spreads out.

en: take sole charge of; bear alone

examples.en: Mr. Kim is solely in charge of counseling new students.
Our team took sole charge of that work.
It is hard to handle childcare all by yourself.

examples.ko: 병원에는 환자 안내를 전담하는 직원이 있어요.
examples.en: The hospital has staff dedicated to guiding patients.

examples.ko: 그 프로젝트는 우리 부서가 전담할 거예요.
examples.en: Our department will handle that project alone.

examples.ko: 번역을 전담해 줄 사람을 찾고 있어요.
examples.en: I'm looking for someone to handle the translation exclusively.

explain: 한 사람이나 한 부서가 어떤 일을 혼자 도맡을 때 써요. '담당하다'는 그 일을 맡는다는 점만 말하고, '전담하다'는 다른 사람은 하지 않고 그 사람만 한다는 느낌이 더해져요. '업무를 전담하다', '전담 부서'처럼 써요.
explain_en: Use it when one person or one department handles a task alone. 담당하다 only says someone is in charge, while 전담하다 adds that nobody else does it. It appears as '업무를 전담하다' and '전담 부서'.

examples.en: The lake is very calm.
I spent a peaceful day in the countryside.
His face looked serene.
I listen to music that calms my mind.
After the storm passed, the sea was calm again.
I'm happy watching the baby sleeping peacefully.

explain: 마음이나 분위기가 흔들리지 않고 편안할 때 써요. '조용하다'는 소리가 없다는 느낌이 강하고, 평온하다는 걱정 없이 안정된 상태에 가까워요. '평화롭다'는 전쟁이나 갈등이 없다는 느낌까지 넓게 써요.
explain_en: Use it when a mind or atmosphere is steady and at ease. 조용하다 focuses on the absence of noise, while 평온하다 is closer to a worry-free, stable state. 평화롭다 goes wider, also suggesting no war or conflict.

en: bomb; carry out an air raid on

examples.en: During the war, planes bombed the city.

examples.ko: 비행기가 다리를 폭격하는 장면이 영화에 나와요.
examples.en: A scene where a plane bombs a bridge appears in the movie.
There was a plan to bomb the enemy base.
The news reported the fact that the village had been bombed.
The planes carried out a bombing run, and the building collapsed.
They bombed first, and then the soldiers moved in.

explain: 비행기 같은 것으로 위에서 폭탄을 떨어뜨려 공격하는 것에 써요. '폭파하다'는 다리나 건물을 터뜨려 부수는 일이라서 달라요. 전쟁 뉴스나 역사 이야기에서 자주 나와요.
explain_en: It is for attacking by dropping bombs from above, with aircraft for example. 폭파하다 is different: it means blowing up a bridge or building. It shows up often in war news and history.

examples.en: I copy good writing by hand into a notebook.
I copied a whole novel by hand.

examples.ko: 시를 필사하면서 한글 쓰기 연습을 했어요.
examples.en: I practiced writing Hangul while copying poems.

examples.ko: 매일 한 쪽씩 필사하는 습관이 생겼어요.
examples.en: I've picked up the habit of copying out a page every day.
In the old days, monks copied scriptures by hand.
I chose a book at the bookstore to copy out.

explain: 좋은 글을 손으로 그대로 베껴 쓰는 일이에요. 요즘은 글쓰기 공부나 마음 정리로 '필사'가 유행이에요. '베끼다'는 숙제나 시험, 표절에도 써서 나쁜 느낌이 있지만, 필사하다는 긍정적인 말이에요.
explain_en: It means copying good writing exactly, by hand. Lately '필사' is popular as a way to study writing or calm the mind. 베끼다 can also be used for copying homework, exams or plagiarism and often sounds negative, while 필사하다 is positive.

examples.en: An internal inspection of the police has begun.
The results of the inspection will be announced next week.

examples.ko: 감찰을 받은 직원은 잠시 일을 쉬었어요.
examples.en: The employee who was investigated took a short break from work.

examples.ko: 학교 안의 문제를 감찰하는 부서가 따로 있어요.
examples.en: There is a separate department that inspects problems inside the school.
The inspector came to check the documents.

examples.ko: 군대에서는 규칙을 지키는지 감찰을 자주 해요.
examples.en: In the military, they often inspect whether rules are followed.

explain: 공공기관, 군대, 경찰 같은 조직 안에서 규칙을 어기지 않았는지 살펴보는 일에 써요. '감사'는 돈과 업무 전체를 살피는 데 많이 쓰고, 감찰은 사람의 행동과 근무 태도를 살피는 데 써요. 일상 대화에서는 거의 안 나와요.
explain_en: It refers to checking, inside public bodies, the military or the police, whether people have broken rules. 감사 (audit) is often about money and overall work, while 감찰 looks at people's conduct and work attitude. It rarely comes up in everyday conversation.
